what_this_is: The clean-kernel SOURCE the newest crystal revalidation record was measured at. Whether a chained BODY drifted is a question only trustc can answer, and the record is its DATED answer; this pins the tree that answer covers, so a pre-push gate and a suite row can decide -- with no Trust compiler and no dump -- whether it still covers the tree in front of them. Derivable: `scripts/crystal_freshness_scope.py --emit`, checked by `--emit --check`. When the record's rev is not a commit here, the kernel tree is read at `kernel_tree_read_at`, a pushed commit whose kernel source digests to the record's clean_kernel_src_sha256 (named once with --witness).
digest_definition: sha256 over, in sorted path order, `<repo-relative path>\0<sha256 of file bytes>\n` for every crates/clean-kernel/src/**/*.rs plus crates/clean-kernel/Cargo.toml, walked from the filesystem.
body_digest_definition: Per chained def_path, sha256 over, in the order `items` lists them, `<anchors joined by ::>\0<the item's CODE text>\n`. An item is located by finding its anchor in a string-, char- and comment-MASKED copy of the file (so a brace in a literal or a comment cannot cut the span), taking the anchor's line start extended back over any #[...] attributes, and ending at the `}` matching the first depth-0 `{` or at the first depth-0 `;`. The item's CODE text is that span with COMMENTS blanked, blank lines dropped and trailing whitespace stripped -- a comment cannot move an emitted instruction -- while string and char literals are kept byte-for-byte, because those are data the compiler emits. `items` pins the body's own item plus the items in that file whose layout or signature its emitted code depends on; `items_why` says which and why. If any item cannot be located UNAMBIGUOUSLY the entry records body_sha256: null and body_extraction: "file-fallback: <reason>", and the check compares `sha256` -- the whole FILE -- for that def_path instead.

bvar_in_range.items_why: three u32 primitives in, bool out; no kernel type in the signature

expr_path_step_clone.items_why: a DERIVED Clone: the body is generated from the enum item and its derive list, so the enum item IS the body's source

flat_flags_contains.items_why: reads FlatFlags' single field; the newtype's shape decides the emitted mask

flat_flags_with.items_why: constructs a FlatFlags from its single field; the newtype's shape decides the emitted or

float_add.items_why: the chained def path is the closure inside it; the closure's argument types come from float_binary_op's bound

float_div.items_why: the chained def path is the closure inside it; the closure's argument types come from float_binary_op's bound

float_mul.items_why: the chained def path is the closure inside it; the closure's argument types come from float_binary_op's bound

float_sub.items_why: the chained def path is the closure inside it; the closure's argument types come from float_binary_op's bound

from_source_system.items_why: maps SourceSystem discriminants to CleanMode discriminants; both enums are load-bearing

get_char_val_trunc.items_why: the chained def path is the `map` closure inside it

has_cubical_layer.items_why: matches on CleanMode; the emitted body switches on the numeric discriminant

has_loose_bvars.items_why: the composition site: it calls loose_bvar_range, which shifts by BVAR_RANGE_SHIFT out of ExprMeta's word -- all three are the emitted body's source

is_valid_char.items_why: one u64 in, bool out; no kernel type in the signature

level_is_zero.items_why: the one chained body that calls: 6 calls into <LevelArc as Deref>::deref, which is inlinable and lives in this file

level_kind_ord.items_why: matches on Level; the emitted body switches on the numeric discriminant. `LevelArc` is pinned for the same reason its sibling `level_is_zero` pins it: `Level` is `Succ(LevelArc) | Max(LevelArc, LevelArc) | IMax(..)`, so Level's layout and niche depend on LevelArc, which lives in this same file. Without it an edit to `struct LevelArc` left this row silently green while `level_is_zero` reddened — a narrowing against the whole-file pin this replaced, and against this map's own doctrine of pinning the items whose layout the emitted code depends on.

meta_tag_shl.items_why: a const item whose body is the shift itself; scoped to its enclosing fn because the test module declares two more consts of that name

node_id_index.items_why: widens NodeId's single field; the newtype's shape decides the emitted cast

simp_priority_value.items_why: matches on SimpPriority and reads its payload; `fn value` is not unique in the file

strict_monads.items_why: one field store into Environment, at an offset chosen by that struct's layout -- a field added there moves this body with its own text unchanged

how_to_re_derive: A CONTENT-SCOPE failure is not refreshed by re-emitting this file. Produce a fresh dump and run scripts/crystal_fixture_freshness.py, commit the new revalidation record, point `record` at it, then --emit.
